non_claim: This packet records the repository census and an action boundary only. It does not assert that Sigstore receives a transfer, is a processor, has a DPF/SCC basis, has Legal/DPO approval, or that cosign-sign.yml should be retained or retired.

scope.question: Decide whether the published GDPR transfer table should name Sigstore at all, given the Trust Center posture that Sigstore never receives customer data and is not a customer-data sub-processor.
out_of_scope: deciding whether image signing is keep or retire

owner_action: UI: Have Legal Counsel and the DPO review the measured row in all four locales together with the Trust Center and generator posture; record a signed disposition without inferring from the workflow's existence or claiming that Sigstore receives no customer data without evidence.
RUN: If the disposition is remove_sigstore_row, update all four locale tables in one reviewed change, retaining the PagerDuty and GitHub recipients and recording the exact diff.
UI: If the disposition is retain_and_document_transfer, provide the legal transfer basis, recipient/service scope, data categories, and effective notice wording; do not reuse this packet as approval.

RUN: Write evidence/owner-actions/B-314/gdpr-sigstore-transfer-decision.json with the four-locale scope, Legal reviewer, DPO reviewer, row disposition, effective date, and source references; then transition B-314 and invert its verifier.

evidence.completion_rule: A signed Legal/DPO disposition covering all four published locale copies is required before the row is removed or retained as a transfer claim.

retry_and_rollback: Retry only against the same notice version and retain the measured diff. An unexecuted draft may be abandoned. A signed legal disposition or published notice requires a superseding review; do not use an unreviewed git revert as rollback.
